# Version 0.45.0

**Date:** Unreleased
**Tag:** `v0.45.0`
**Range:** `v0.44.0..master`

## Highlights

- **Row edits no longer hit the wrong row on large integer keys.** JavaScript
  rounds integers above 2^53, so a snowflake id or a CockroachDB
  `unique_rowid()` key came back as a different number and an edit or delete
  could target another row. Those values now reach the app as strings and keep
  every digit.

## Features

- **Settings view.** Settings move out of the sidebar panel into a full view.
  All sections sit in one scroll with section headers and a navigation that
  follows the section in view. Search filters the setting rows in place,
  highlights matches and counts them per section; `Enter` jumps to the first
  match, `Esc` clears and `/` focuses search. Rows, theme swatches and controls
  are more compact and use theme tokens, so light themes work.
- **Schema map redesign.** A table list on the left, grouped by connected
  tables or by schema, with search that also matches columns. Tables are laid
  out in layers so referenced tables sit left of the tables that point at
  them. Connectors run from the foreign key column to the referenced key and
  light up for the selected table; switch between flowing, dashed and solid
  with `L`. The details panel shows a schema overview (most referenced tables,
  missing primary keys, unindexed foreign keys) or, for a selected table, its
  facts, references, checks, columns and SQL or Drizzle definition. New
  toolbar with view and arrange modes, minimap, fit and export. Keys: `/`
  search, `Esc` clear, `F` fit, `E` arrange, `M` minimap, `+` `-` `0` zoom.
- **Schema diff redesign.** The ORM cockpit diff shows a summary of what the
  migration does, a risk level per table, include checkboxes and a risk
  filter. The SQL preview is rebuilt from the real migration as tables are
  included or excluded, and hovering a change highlights its statement.
  Destructive and review statements still need an explicit opt-in.
- **Docker containers view redesign.** Dense rows grouped by status with arrow
  key navigation, one View menu for filter and sort, and a details pane with
  the connection string, live CPU and memory sparklines, ports, masked
  environment variables, volumes, logs and shell. A new container drawer has
  quick start templates and a free port lookup.
- **Duplicate many rows at once.** Duplicating a selection copies all rows in
  one command, inside a transaction where the engine allows it.
- **Batched cell edits and row inserts.** Edits and inserts across many rows go
  to the database together, with undo, and atomically on SQLite and
  PostgreSQL.
- **New side rail.** A custom icon set with a sliding indicator for the active
  view. Hovering or focusing a rail item preloads that view.
- **Animated source icons in the connection dialog.** Database engines, Files,
  Cloudflare D1 and PostHog get their own glyphs with a short hover motion.
  Provider logos stay as they are. Reduced motion turns the motion off.
- **SQL console seeding.** Opening a connection restores relevant queries, with
  a table-based fallback that skips migration bookkeeping tables.
- **More install channels and platforms.** macOS ships as one universal DMG,
  so Intel Macs install and update too. Linux arm64 and Windows arm64 builds
  are added on a best effort basis. New signed DNF/YUM and Flatpak
  repositories, Scoop and Nix packages, and APT now serves arm64 as well.
- **Redis and Valkey** use the shared illustrated empty states.

## Fixes

- Snap and Flatpak shipped a development build that loaded
  `localhost:1420` instead of the bundled frontend. Snap now builds with
  `custom-protocol` and Flatpak wraps the released `.deb`.
- README install instructions pointed at a Homebrew tap and APT host that did
  not exist, and at an `.msi` that is not built.
- PostgreSQL key-value edits cast text parameters to the column type.
- Docker and command palette stay usable while availability checks are still
  running.
- Docker stats handle streamed output and stopping containers.
- Migration metadata tables are no longer picked as the default query target.

## Technical

- The publish gate now requires the full x86_64 and macOS asset set, including
  `.deb`, `.rpm`, the Linux tarball and checksums. `latest.json` adds
  `darwin-x86_64`.
- 64-bit integers outside the JavaScript safe range are serialised as strings
  in result rows. Every write path already accepted string-encoded integers.
- New `duplicate_rows` command on the write adapter, with a transactional
  override for adapters that own a single connection, and a write matrix test
  suite across the engines.
- Docker container inspection runs as one command, and Docker data preloads
  with its view chunk. Dialog and assistant chunks preload when idle.
- React Flow inherits the app colour scheme, so the schema map canvas no longer
  pulls in light theme tokens in dark mode.
